answer: Sybil resistance works like pricing a comet pass: a new agent identity must post a per-epoch bond that decays only as it survives real challenges, and each vouching peer stakes a vertex of its own graph on the newcomer — forfeit if the identity is later proven fake. Voting weight stays proportional to bonded epochs survived, not accounts held, so a farm splitting one wallet into a crystal of clones gains nothing: every clone starts the same expensive clock, and collusion between vouchers is punished on the public pledge graph. Cost scales with identities; honesty just waits.
